mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__flo.mechanism: Mangrove belts strongly reduce coastal flooding by breaking waves and, more weakly, lowering surge water as it passes through the forest [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3]. Existing mangroves cut wave heights by 31% in a meta-analysis of field measurements [ev_frmg_nara16_1], and measured surge peaks fall by 5 to 50 centimetres per kilometre of mangrove [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1]. A global model finds that losing current mangroves would flood 28% more people each year [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1], and a Philippine model gives 24% more [ev_flood_hazard_wbphl17_1]. In India and Bangladesh, villages sheltered by existing mangrove forest took less salt water and flood water after super cyclones [ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7, ev_flood_hazard_akber18_7]. The avoided damage has been put in money terms: in Orissa mangroves protected houses worth USD 1218 per hectare of forest in a single cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and mangroves in front of sea dykes cut repair costs by 20–30% [ev_avoided_damage_value_badola05_10]. Of restoration projects reviewed, 50% report better storm protection [ev_frmg_nara16_5]. In New Zealand, an existing mangrove forest about 1 km wide with no drainage channels lowered peak water by about 24 cm per km [ev_flood_hazard_montgomery18_1], and a global model of restoring all restorable mangroves in front of dikes finds about 140,000 fewer people (3%) affected by flooding each year [ev_flood_hazard_tiggeloven26_1]. A Caribbean model of flood protection finds many coastlines where mangroves give long-term flood protection worth hundreds of thousands of dollars per hectare, so that restoration near Port au Prince, Haiti, costing less than $168,000 per hectare would still pay back [ev_avoided_damage_value_beck22_2].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__flo.conditionality: Most of this evidence describes existing forest, so it shows what keeping mangroves protects; that a planted belt will do the same is assumed [ev_frmg_nara16_1, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbphl17_1, ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7]. Surge and tidal water is lowered much less than waves [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3], and a World Bank Bangladesh model finds mangroves change total design water level by less than 4% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1]. The village surveys are small and their authors call them only indicative [ev_flood_hazard_badola05_7, ev_flood_hazard_akber18_7], and the money values are avoided damage to society, not income to the households working the coast [ev_economic_return_das11_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_1]. One source runs against the practice: in Orissa, coastal land was worth more in other uses than the house protection mangroves gave, so on that basis alone rehabilitation could not be justified [ev_economic_return_das11_2]. The restoration-specific results are self-reported or modelled with fully grown trees assumed [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2, ev_flood_hazard_dasgupta19_1, ev_avoided_damage_value_wbphl17_2]. In a similar New Zealand forest cut by drainage channels there was no measurable drop in water level [ev_flood_hazard_montgomery18_2]. The global restoration model assumes working dikes behind every restored area and leaves out cyclone damage to the mangroves [ev_flood_hazard_tiggeloven26_1]. The Caribbean figure is a model of avoided direct damage to property, so it is a break-even value for the public rather than a measured drop in flooding [ev_avoided_damage_value_beck22_2].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__foo.mechanism: Restored mangroves give fish, crabs and shellfish places to breed and shelter. In a rehabilitated mangrove basin in Java, Indonesia, fishing for finfish grew from practically zero to a profitable livelihood [ev_fish_catch_debrot22_1]; in Aceh, crabs and oysters increased after planting and women no longer had to travel up to 3 km to gather oysters [ev_fish_catch_wibsua08_3]; and in Sri Lankan lagoon villages, more participation in mangrove restoration was linked to higher fish production per boat [ev_fish_catch_sathi24_2]. In Viet Nam the value of wild catch rises with mangrove density, from US$991/ha/year where cover is under 30% to US$3,248/ha/year where it is over 70% [ev_fish_catch_wbicr6719_7], and in Indonesia fisheries make up almost 64% of the value mangroves provide in products [ev_fish_catch_vzanten25_1].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__foo.conditionality: Catch and harvest are a stand-in for food security; no study measures diets or hunger. The Viet Nam and Indonesia values describe existing mangrove and are transferred from other studies, not measured at restored sites [ev_fish_catch_wbicr6719_7, ev_fish_catch_vzanten25_1]. The Java and Aceh accounts have no comparison site and the Aceh one is anecdotal and written by the implementer [ev_fish_catch_debrot22_1, ev_fish_catch_wibsua08_3]; the Sri Lankan link is only weakly significant [ev_fish_catch_sathi24_2]; and a Senegal model simply assumes a 3.0% gain in fishery output [ev_fish_catch_iisd26_3].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__pro.mechanism: The evidence points to a small production gain, though the support is weak, mostly in pond farming next to the mangroves. A World Bank project report in Viet Nam cites studies finding that improved mangrove forest more than 5 years old raised aquaculture values by US$359.7/ha and US$276.6/ha, and by US$1,436.8/ha/year in a third study [ev_agricultural_production_value_wbicr6719_4, ev_agricultural_production_value_wbicr6719_5, ev_agricultural_production_value_wbicr6719_6]. A Senegal model assumes mangrove restoration raises farm productivity by 2.3% [ev_crop_yield_iisd26_5]. Other findings point the other way, for pond farming. In northern Java, Indonesia, the authors judge that mangroves planted on pond walls and inside ponds hamper pond upkeep, and that their leaf litter and shade lower pond yield [ev_aquaculture_yield_bosma20_2]. In the Philippines, a study citing earlier work notes that turning leased brackish fishponds back into mangrove gives up their fish output (these ponds average 1.06 t/ha), although the cited author judges the national loss small and easily replaced [ev_aquaculture_yield_ferrer11_2].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__pro.conditionality: Both pond findings say mangroves in ponds, or in place of ponds, lower pond yield [ev_aquaculture_yield_bosma20_2, ev_aquaculture_yield_ferrer11_2]. No study here measures pond yield with and without mangroves at a similar level of farming intensity, so the size of that loss is unknown. None of the gains is measured at a project site either: the Viet Nam figures are borrowed from other studies and the Senegal figure is a model assumption [ev_agricultural_production_value_wbicr6719_6, ev_crop_yield_iisd26_5]. A paddy yield comparison from Bhitarkanika, India, is held out because it measures what an existing forest protected in a cyclone year, not what restoration adds to normal yields [ev_crop_yield_badola05_6].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__rur.mechanism: Mangrove restoration reaches coastal households mainly through fish, crabs and shellfish. In northern Viet Nam mangroves raised shellfish and oyster yields per hectare by 209-789 per cent [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]; in Java a new finfish fishery earns fishers about 1.05 USD per hour [ev_household_income_debrot22_2]; a Philippine survey suggests replanted mangroves add USD 564–2316/ha/y to local incomes [ev_household_income_debrot22_3]; and in Sri Lankan lagoon villages more participation in restoration was linked to more fish per boat [ev_fish_catch_sathi24_2]. Most appraisals of the planting find benefits above costs, including a global meta-analysis, commune studies in Viet Nam and Mexican pilot sites [ev_economic_return_su21_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_frmg_mxicr_1], and a Bangladesh appraisal finds mangrove-and-aquaculture systems profitable once mature [ev_economic_return_rahman18_6]. In Gujarat, India, 34 of 227 households surveyed reported higher fishing income after mangrove planting [ev_household_income_becklange16_1], and in the Philippines a costing of letting disused fishponds revert to mangrove gives benefit-cost ratios of 4.53 to 4.69 [ev_economic_return_ferrer11_1].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__rur.conditionality: No study measures poverty against a comparison; the evidence is yields, catches and appraisals, many projected or reported by implementers [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1, ev_frmg_erw09_1, ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. The same Bangladesh appraisal projects losses for most landowners in the first years, a harm counted against the practice [ev_economic_return_rahman18_4, ev_economic_return_rahman18_5]. Results whose value goes to society are held out: a World Bank project in Viet Nam returned only 3.6 percent without carbon [ev_economic_return_wbicr6719_3], a Senegal model's ratios of 2.27 to 5.71 come mostly from avoided damage [ev_economic_return_iisd26_7], Indonesian restoration loses money where land is valuable [ev_economic_return_wbidn22_3], and breakwater savings go to the public [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. Fishery values from existing mangroves in Viet Nam and Indonesia are also held out because they describe standing forest, not restoration [ev_fish_catch_wbicr6719_7, ev_fish_catch_vzanten25_1]. The Gujarat result is household recall with no comparison villages, from grey literature [ev_household_income_becklange16_1], and the Philippine benefits are borrowed from a Thai valuation rather than measured [ev_economic_return_ferrer11_1]. A global model giving benefit-cost ratios between 3 and 6 for restoring mangroves in front of dikes is held out, because its benefit is avoided flood damage to buildings, which goes to society [ev_economic_return_tiggeloven26_2]. A Caribbean model finding that flood-protection benefits outweigh restoration costs along 181 coastal units in 20 countries and territories is held out for the same reason [ev_economic_return_beck22_1].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__soi.mechanism: Mangroves moderately reduce coastal erosion: they slow water and trap sediment, so the coast builds up instead of washing away; their roots and trunks make water drop its sediment [ev_mg_erosion_sp14_20261030, ev_mg_sediment_sp14_20261030, ev_sediment_retention_hutchfish14_2]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta, project monitoring reports coastal erosion reduced by 40 percent in Ca Mau because of replanted mangroves [ev_frmg_vnppar_1], and evaluators found mangroves had turned the Soc Trang coast into an area that builds up [ev_frmg_vnppar_2]. A World Bank model for Bangladesh finds mangrove belts in front of embankments reduce the force of water on the embankment base by 7%-16% for narrow belts and 45%-72% for wide ones [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_2]. In Indonesia, permeable brushwood dams that let mangroves return trapped about 0.5 m of sediment in four months while the coast kept eroding elsewhere [ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_1]. In Bangladesh, government mangrove planting on coastal mudflats is reported to have been very effective in building land, with rapid sediment build-up [ev_sediment_retention_becklange16_1]. Detailed observations of a fringe mangrove forest in Vietnam, part of it planted, found the mangroves engineer the landscape, favouring sediment deposition and dissipating waves [ev_sediment_retention_fagh17_5].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__soi.conditionality: Results depend on siting and survival: in parts of Bac Lieu replanted mangroves washed away and erosion continued [ev_frmg_vnppar_2], and in Indonesia mangroves planted on pond dykes and inside ponds did not stop the dykes being destroyed by spring tides and storms [ev_erosion_hazard_bosma20_1]. The Vietnam figures are uncontrolled monitoring [ev_frmg_vnppar_1], the Bangladesh embankment result is a model of existing mangrove belts from grey literature [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1], the coastal-defence manual describes what existing mangroves do [ev_mg_erosion_sp14_20261030], project staff claims and practitioner ratings from Bangladesh add no measurement [ev_erosion_hazard_ahammad13_2, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4300_2019_surface_runoff], and the dam results come from authors linked to the implementers [ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_1, ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_5]. There is no controlled measurement of erosion under mangrove restoration. The Bangladesh account is a grey-literature summary, mostly of planting on newly formed land [ev_sediment_retention_becklange16_1]. The Vietnam fringe observations describe shoreline building with no size given [ev_sediment_retention_fagh17_5].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__wat.mechanism: The evidence points to a benefit for water quality, but no source says how large. A review reports that restored mangrove sites in southern Chinese estuaries hold more trace metals in their mud than nearby bare areas; in Yundang Lagoon, for example, copper was 59.82 µg/g in restored areas against 54.41 µg/g in bare areas [ev_trace_metal_retention_uddin24_2]. Coastal defence guidance states that mangroves, with the algae, bacteria and filter-feeding animals living among them, remove extra nutrients from coastal water [ev_mg_nutrients_sp14_20261030].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__wat.conditionality: The metal finding is second-hand, from a review, and concerns metals held in the mud rather than measured changes in the water [ev_trace_metal_retention_uddin24_2]. The nutrient finding describes what existing mangrove forest does, not what restored stands achieve [ev_mg_nutrients_sp14_20261030]. One finding points to a risk: a cited Australian study found that crabs in urban restored mangroves carried more trace metals in their bodies than crabs in natural mangroves, and the authors suggest a higher risk from crabs in restored sites [ev_trace_metal_in_biota_uddin24_3]. That compares restored with natural forest, not with the bare site before restoration, so it does not set the rating.

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__win.mechanism: Mangroves give strong shelter from cyclone wind, waves and surge to what lies behind them. Planted mangroves in Hainan, China, cut mean wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1], and in northern Viet Nam planting is credited with keeping a sea dyke undamaged in a 2005 typhoon and cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. Studies of existing forest show the same protection: in Orissa, India, villages with wider mangroves had fewer deaths in the 1999 super cyclone [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_2]; in Bhitarkanika the sheltered village had lower losses per household, less house damage and a higher cyclone-year paddy yield than the unprotected village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_2, ev_crop_yield_badola05_6]; and in Bangladesh, households sheltered by the Sundarbans recalled almost half the total loss of unsheltered households after cyclone Sidr [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_1], while a separate survey found mean Sidr damage of US$1,327 per household behind the forest against US$1,478 elsewhere [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. In Central America, wider mangrove belts meant smaller losses of economic activity after hurricanes [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_delvalle20_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_hochard19_1]. After community mangrove planting in Gujarat, India, 74 of 227 households surveyed reported reduced cyclone and storm damage [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__win.conditionality: Most of this evidence measures what keeping existing mangrove forest protects, not what planting achieves; the planted-stand results from Viet Nam are uncontrolled before-and-after reports by evaluators of the implementing programme [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1]. Some measured results show no benefit or the reverse, and these lower the rating: in Orissa no mangrove effect on fully collapsed houses was seen near the coast [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_2], protection was smaller for larger surges [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_3], Bhitarkanika livestock losses were higher in the mangrove village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_4], and in the Sundarbans tree damage and livestock losses were about the same with or without the forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_4]. The village surveys are small, rely on recall, and have unprotected sites closer to the storm path [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_1]. In the newer Sundarbans survey households behind the forest also spent more on protecting themselves and fewer lived inside an embankment, so the damage gap is not all due to the mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. A World Bank evaluation in the Mekong Delta found farming protected where planting succeeded but the coastline moving inland where seedlings failed [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The Gujarat result is household recall with no comparison villages, from grey literature [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__win.mechanism: For rainfed cropping the most direct evidence is a cyclone-year paddy yield of 1479.5 kg ha−1 in the Bhitarkanika village sheltered by the mangrove forest against 531 kg ha−1 in the unprotected village [ev_crop_yield_badola05_6], Sundarbans households in a sheltered polder recalling a much smaller loss of their standing crop after cyclone Sidr [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_5], and a Mekong Delta evaluation reporting farming protected from storms, wind and salt where mangrove reforestation succeeded [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The rest of the evidence covers people, houses and economic activity: planted mangroves in Hainan, China, cut wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]; in Orissa wider mangroves meant fewer cyclone deaths [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1]; and a separate Bangladesh survey found mean Sidr damage of US$1,327 per household behind the Sundarbans against US$1,478 elsewhere [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. After community mangrove planting in Gujarat, India, 74 of 227 households surveyed reported reduced cyclone and storm damage [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__win.conditionality: The crop comparisons describe existing forest, not planted stands, and are single-cyclone village surveys: the Bhitarkanika comparison has no normal-year yield per village, so part of the gap may be a difference in the land itself [ev_crop_yield_badola05_6], and the unsheltered Sundarbans polder farmed larger paddy fields and lay closer to the storm path [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_5]. Some results show no benefit or the reverse, and these lower the rating: tree and livestock losses were about the same with or without the Sundarbans [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_4], and Bhitarkanika livestock losses were higher in the mangrove village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_4]. Households behind the Sundarbans also spent more on protecting themselves, so not all of their smaller damage is due to the forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. In the Mekong Delta, where seedlings were planted too small and not monitored, the coastline moved inland instead [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The Gujarat result is household recall with no comparison villages, from grey literature [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1].

mangrove_restoration__water_quality_risk.mechanism: There is not enough evidence to rate this. The only finding is a review reporting that restored mangrove sites in southern Chinese estuaries hold more trace metals in their mud than nearby bare areas; in Yundang Lagoon, for example, copper was 59.82 µg/g in restored areas against 54.41 µg/g in bare areas [ev_trace_metal_retention_uddin24_2].
mangrove_restoration__water_quality_risk.conditionality: This is a single review citing other studies, about metals held in the mud rather than measured changes in the water [ev_trace_metal_retention_uddin24_2]. A second independent source, or a measured change in water quality at a restored site, is needed before a rating can be given.

mangrove_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.mechanism: Planted mangroves shelter what lies behind them from cyclone wind and waves. Planted mangroves in Hainan, China, cut mean wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons, a result cited in a review [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. In northern Viet Nam, mangrove planting is credited with keeping a sea dyke undamaged in a 2005 typhoon and cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. In Gujarat, India, 74 of 227 households surveyed reported reduced cyclone and storm damage after mangrove planting [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1], project staff in coastal Bangladesh state that mangrove afforestation has reduced loss of life and property in cyclones [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1], and a World Bank evaluation in the Mekong Delta finds farming protected from storms, wind and salt where reforestation succeeded [ev_frmg_vnppar_8].
mangrove_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.conditionality: Every unit here concerns planting, but none is a controlled measurement: the Viet Nam results are before-and-after reports by evaluators of the implementing programme [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1], the Gujarat result is what households recalled, with no comparison villages, reported in grey literature [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1], the Bangladesh statement comes from the project's own staff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1], and the Hainan figure is cited second-hand [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. None of the evidence is from a severe or extreme cyclone. The same Mekong evaluation found the coastline moving inland where seedlings were planted too small and not monitored, so the benefit depends on the planting succeeding [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. Part of the protection falls beyond the farm, on dykes, ponds and villages.

mangrove_restoration__wind_cyclone__all_.mechanism: In lower-income settings the evidence is two reports from planting programmes. In Gujarat, India, 74 of 227 households surveyed reported reduced cyclone and storm damage after mangrove planting [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1], and project staff in coastal Bangladesh state that mangrove afforestation has reduced loss of life and property in tropical cyclones [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1].
mangrove_restoration__wind_cyclone__all_.conditionality: Both point to less damage but neither says how much. The Gujarat result is what households recalled, with no comparison villages and no named storm, reported in grey literature [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_becklange16_1], and the Bangladesh statement is the implementing project's own claim with no monitoring described [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1]. Neither covers a severe or extreme cyclone.
